title: 'Reset All to 0 deg' wipes an imported horizon with no confirmation, one click from the Import button
reasoning: The claimed code is present. location_settings.dart:438 routes the button through `_resetHorizon(horizonProfile)` and _resetHorizon (lines 765-799) computes `hasSurvey = current.sampleCount >= 2` and `hasMask = horizonDirections.any((dir) => current.altitudeAt(dir) > 0)`, showing a destructive ConfirmDialog whenever either is true and returning early on decline. I checked the guard predicate against the model rather than trusting it: HorizonProfile._normalizeSamples (settings_provider.dart:459) drops sample lists shorter than 2, so a plain 8-sector mask has sampleCount 0 and the 'already flat, no dialog' branch is genuinely reachable - the guard is not silently always-on noise. The confirm path writes `LegacyHorizonProfile(reset).toJson()` with the default empty samples list, so confirming really does clear the survey and not just the eight sectors. I also looked for a second unguarded destruction path: _updateHorizonProfile (line 810) writes a samples-less JSON when a sector box is edited, which does discard an imported survey - but that is disclosed in place at lines 345-352 ('editing any of them replaces the survey with your eight values'), so it is a stated consequence of a deliberate edit, not the misclick this finding is about.
evidence: Sever test: I replaced `onPressed: () => _resetHorizon(horizonProfile)` at location_settings.dart:438 with a direct `setHorizonProfileJson(flat)` write - the pre-fix behaviour - and location_horizon_reset_guard_test.dart went from 5/5 green to 1 passed / 4 FAILED ('Found 0 widgets with text "Reset the horizon mask?"' at test lines 78 and 119; the cancel and confirm cases fail on the missing dialog too). Restoring the call site returned it to 5/5. The test is wired to the production call site, not merely to logic inside _resetHorizon.

title: Storage path fields look like editable text inputs but silently ignore typing
reasoning: The code matches the claim in both halves. settings_color_and_path_inputs.dart:187 defines `_editable => widget.onPathEntered != null`; build() (line 289) branches to a real TextField inside the bordered/filled Container when editable and to a bare Padding+Text with no border, no fill and no 'Not set' hint box when not, so the three read-only call sites I checked (plate_solving_settings_screen.dart:392/405/443 and phd2_guiding_settings.dart:324, none of which pass onPathEntered) genuinely stop looking like inputs. Commit is wired twice - `onSubmitted: (_) => _commit()` at line 315 and a FocusNode listener at line 194/225 that commits on focus loss - with a `_committing` re-entrancy guard so the unfocus that Flutter performs after submit cannot double-fire, and a `finally` block (line 251) that snaps the controller back to widget.path whenever the handler refused. Validation is in _enterPath (file_path_settings.dart:228-295) and is real, not decorative: empty and `!p.isAbsolute` are refused with a reason, remote mode refuses the non-'image' keys before writing, and an unreachable folder goes through ConfirmDialog 'Store anyway' rather than being silently stored - which preserves the finding's own NAS/UNC use case. The probe is behind storageDirectoryProbeProvider as claimed. One residual I considered and did not count as a defect: in remote mode the Sequences row still renders an editable TextField whose content is always refused, which is the same shape as the original complaint - but it is refused OUT LOUD ('This path can only be changed on the host machine.') rather than silently, the fixer states this behaviour explicitly, and turning it into a label would remove the only place that explains why.
evidence: Sever test: I deleted `onPathEntered:` from the Image output row (file_path_settings.dart:347) and file_path_typed_path_test.dart went from 6/6 to 1 passed / 5 FAILED; restoring it returned 6/6. I did not trust the 'commits on focus loss' half of the claim, which the shipped test did not exercise at all (it only sent TextInputAction.done), so I added 'leaving the field commits the typed path' - enterText with no Enter, then tap the Sequences field to move focus - and it passes against the production code and fails under the sever. Tests run green: file_path_typed_path_test.dart (6/6), file_path_settings_authority_test.dart, settings_picker_controls_test.dart.
repairSummary: Added 'leaving the field commits the typed path' to packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/file_path_typed_path_test.dart (plus a _sequencesField() finder). The shipped tests covered only the Enter path, so a fix that wired onSubmitted and not the FocusNode listener would have passed while the operator who types a path and clicks the next box still loses it silently - the original finding one keystroke away. The new case fails if the focus-loss commit is removed.

title: At a ~900px window the status bar shows three identical 'Disconnected' chips with no device names
reasoning: The claimed code is there. pill_widgets.dart:47 defines `_denseText => widget.dense && !widget.isConnected ? widget.label : widget.value`, the label Text is still suppressed in the dense branch (line 114) and the value Text now renders _denseText (line 132) in textSecondary while disconnected. I checked the four call sites in status_bar.dart (lines 261-321): each passes a distinct label ('Camera', 'Mount', 'Guider', 'Focus') and `dense: dense`, so no pill is left behind - the recurring INCOMPLETE shape here would have been a fifth pill still repeating the state, and there is none. The disconnected values really were identical: Camera/Mount/Guider all resolve to l10n 'disconnected'; Focus resolved to '---', so its dense text goes from three dashes to 'Focus', slightly wider but strictly more informative. Nothing is lost, as claimed: the muted dot (line 52), the muted icon (line 103) and the Tooltip '${label}: ${value}' (line 64) all still carry the state. One inaccuracy in the summary, not in the code: it calls this the 'sub-1280 px' pill, but `dense` is gated on BreakpointTokens.breakpointDesktop, which is 1024.0, not 1280 (breakpointDesktopWide is the 1280 one). The reported condition (~900 px) is below 1024 either way, so the fix does apply where the finding was observed - but anyone reading the summary would place the threshold 256 px too high.
evidence: Sever test: I collapsed `_denseText` back to `widget.value` (the pre-fix expression) and status_bar_overflow_test.dart went from 7/7 to 6 passed / 1 FAILED - 'a narrow bar names the devices instead of repeating the state'. Restoring it returned 7/7. The test pins both directions: at 800x600 it requires all four labels present and 'Disconnected' absent, and at 2600x900 it requires the labels AND findsNWidgets(3) 'Disconnected', so a fix that simply deleted the state text everywhere would fail. Regression sweep: the whole test/screens/shell/ directory is green (93/93). Note the finding's secondary complaint (the Focus chip scrolling out of the group) is NOT closed - at 800 test px maxScrollExtent is still greater than zero and the pill group still scrolls - but the summary only claims to mitigate it, and the fade marker for the overflow is separately tested.

title: Files & Storage refuses to name the application data folder, so a user cannot find their own database, logs or backups
reasoning: Half the fix is real and half of it is a NEW false claim. The real half: applicationDataPathProvider (file_path_settings.dart:67) resolves `(await resolveDefaultDatabaseFile()).parent.path` and _AppDataFolderRow renders it with an 'Open folder'/'Copy path' button through appDataFolderRevealerProvider, and the SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR pinned line is gated on the variable actually being set (skotiqDatabaseDirEnv is 'SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR', connection.dart:6). The quarantine claim also checks out - integrity_check.dart:75 rotates corrupt databases to `skotiq-corrupt-*` in the SAME directory as skotiq.db. The false half is the logs: the shipped subtitle said this folder contains 'skotiq.db, the logs folder, and any recovered or quarantined database files. This is what to attach to a bug report.' It does not contain the logs folder. Two DIFFERENT resolvers are involved: resolveDefaultDatabaseFile (connection.dart:12) returns <documents>/Skotiq/skotiq.db or $SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR, while LoggingService._initializeImpl (logging_service.dart:195-200) writes `${resolveSkotiqDataDirectory()}/logs`, and resolveSkotiqDataDirectory (skotiq_data_directory.dart:22) returns $SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR or getApplicationSupportDirectory() - on Linux ~/Documents/Skotiq versus ~/.local/share/<app>. apps/desktop/lib/desktop_logging_init.dart:83 confirms the same root. So the row, which is TITLED 'Database and logs', named one folder, asserted the logs were in it, and told the operator that was what to attach to a bug report - a folder with no logs in it. That is exactly the campaign's recurring shape: one false claim ('managed automatically', i.e. we will not say) swapped for a different, harder-to-catch false claim. The finding itself asks for the logs to be findable, so removing the sentence would not close it either.
evidence: I traced both resolvers to their definitions rather than inferring from the row text, and confirmed the log root is application-support / SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR in two independent places (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/logging_service.dart:195 and apps/desktop/lib/desktop_logging_init.dart:70-84). Repair verification: with the repair in place file_path_typed_path_test.dart is 7/7; when I temporarily restored the old 'the logs folder,' sentence and deleted the 'Open logs' button, the new case failed with "Expected: no matching candidates / Actual: Found 1 widget with text containing 'the logs folder,'". flutter analyze on the two edited files: no issues.
repairSummary: In packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/file_path_settings.dart: added applicationLogPathProvider (resolveSkotiqDataDirectory() + '/logs' - the same path LoggingService writes to), dropped 'the logs folder' from the database-folder contents sentence, added a 'Logs: <path>' line and an 'Open logs' / 'Copy logs path' button beside the existing one (the trailing widget became a Wrap, matching the Backups row one line below), and changed the bug-report instruction to 'Attach both folders to a bug report.' Added 'the logs folder is named separately and can be opened' to file_path_typed_path_test.dart, which asserts the logs path is shown, that the old 'the logs folder,' claim is gone, and that the button reveals the log directory and not the database directory.

title: Settings search returns section names only - it never shows or scrolls to the row that matched
reasoning: The claimed machinery is all present and works for real SettingRows: settings_screen.dart:78 SettingsSearchResult, :136 matchingSettingsRows (row-shape filter + word-boundary token test + shortest-first, limit 3), :287 the results are built with the rows kept, _DesktopSearchResults (:766) and _MobileSearchResults (:1014) both render them as indented tappable _SearchRowResult entries, _selectSection (:235) carries the rowTitle and clears it on a 4 s timer, and both detail panes are wrapped in SettingsRowHighlight (:415 mobile, :502 desktop) which SettingRow consumes at settings_section_and_row.dart:235 to run Scrollable.ensureVisible in a post-frame callback and tint itself. What it misses is the case its OWN doc comment says the row results exist to end. isRowShapedSettingsTerm screens out prose, but nothing screens out a SettingsSection HEADING, and the generated index is full of them: I ran the real matcher over the real index and got 'Dithering' and 'Meridian Flip' for the Sequencer entry, 'Notification Events' for Notifications, 'Dark Frame' for Calibration, 'Dark Library' for the dark library, 'Theme' for Appearance. None of those is a SettingRow - sequencer_settings.dart:650 and :214, notification_settings.dart:291, calibration_settings.dart:189 are all SettingsSection(title:), and dark_library_settings.dart:43 / notification_settings.dart:255 are SettingsPage(title:). SettingsSection was a bare Text with no highlight participation, so tapping one of those results opened the page at the top and marked nothing - verbatim the finding being closed. It is not an edge case: for the query 'meridian flip' the ONLY row result offered under Sequencer was the heading, so the entire promise of the feature failed on that query. Also 'Notifications' was offered as a row indented under the section named 'Notifications', which is pure noise. Both are now repaired.
evidence: Reproduction: a widget test that searched 'dither', tapped the sidebar result 'Dithering' and asked whether the detail-pane heading was tinted printed 'sidebar Dithering: 1 / detail Dithering: 1 / highlighted: false' and failed on expect(..., isTrue). After the repair the same test prints highlighted: true. Sever test of the ORIGINAL fix (before repair): replacing SettingsSearchResult(section, matchingSettingsRows(section, tokens)) with SettingsSearchResult(section, const []) at settings_screen.dart:287 took settings_search_row_target_test.dart from 3/3 to 0 passed / 3 FAILED; separately setting rowTitle: null on the desktop SettingsRowHighlight took it to 1 passed / 2 FAILED. Restoring gave 3/3. So the shipped tests are wired to the production call sites, they just did not cover headings. Sever test of MY repair: reverting the _HighlightedRow wrapper in SettingsSection makes the new heading case fail (full settings directory: 454 passed / 3 failed, the 3rd being my new test) while the rest stays green. Regression sweep: `flutter test test/screens/settings` is 453-455 passing across three runs; the only consistent failure is captures_landscape_test.dart, which fails identically WITH my edit reverted (Golden 'captures/settings_android_landscape_932x430.png' pixel test 4.38%) - the known Windows-captured-goldens-on-Linux debt, not mine. One run showed 7 extra failures (about_system_information, pairing_*, backup_restore_notice, equipment_profile_import_authority) but they pass in isolation both with and without my edit and did not recur on re-run: that is the known drift 'created SkotiqDatabase multiple times' concurrency flake in this directory, not a regression. flutter analyze on both edited lib files: No issues found.
repairSummary: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/settings_widgets/settings_section_and_row.dart: SettingsSection's heading Text is now wrapped in the same _HighlightedRow the rows use, so a search result that names a section HEADING scrolls to it and tints it instead of opening the page at the top and marking nothing (layout-neutral - AnimatedContainer with a transparent colour when inactive). packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/settings_screen.dart: matchingSettingsRows now skips any indexed term equal to the section's own label, so 'Notifications' is no longer offered as a row indented beneath the section called Notifications. Added two cases to test/screens/settings/settings_search_row_target_test.dart - 'a matched SECTION HEADING is revealed too, not just rows' (searches 'dither', taps the 'Dithering' result, asserts the heading is on screen AND tinted; fails if the wrapper is reverted) and 'a term identical to the section name is not offered as a row'. Also deleted the fixer's leftover debug file test/screens/settings/tmp_probe_search_rows_test.dart, which only print()ed the index, and fixed the two analyzer infos dart format surfaced in settings_screen.dart.

title: The latitude and longitude fields silently discard any coordinate that is not already decimal degrees
reasoning: The behavioural core is real and correct. SettingsNumberInput gained `parse` (settings_text_and_number_inputs.dart:260); _parseText (:341) routes through it instead of double.tryParse, build() (:456) sets `custom = widget.parse != null` and genuinely LIFTS the formatter (`inputFormatters: custom ? const [] : [_numberFormatter]`, :461) and switches keyboardType to TextInputType.text, so a pasted DMS string is no longer swallowed; _commit (:359) re-formats to decimal degrees so the operator sees what was read. location_settings.dart:146 and :174 supply it with the right maxDegrees/hemispheres, and parseSiteAngle (:970) reads decimal, D M S, D:M:S, degree/prime/double-prime marks, d/m/s letters and a leading or trailing hemisphere, refusing out-of-range, >3 components, a fraction before the last component, minutes/seconds >= 60, and a sign that contradicts the hemisphere. I ran 21 adversarial inputs through the real function; the refusals all landed where the summary says. TWO things were wrong. (1) The summary asserts 'the search-index generator only indexes `title:`, so no regeneration was needed'. That is false, and the SAME WAVE's own comment in settings_screen.dart:90-97 says so: the generator's pattern is `title:\s*'...'` with no left word boundary, so every `subtitle:` is indexed. Both coordinate subtitles were reworded, and `dart run tools/production/settings_search_index_gen.dart --check` reported the index STALE. The consequences were both directions of wrong: searching 'DMS' or 'decimal degrees' reached nothing (the new capability was undiscoverable through the search box the same wave was rebuilding), and the index still carried the DELETED strings 'Positive for North, negative for South' and 'Positive for East, negative for West' - each 6 words and 38 characters, i.e. row-shaped by isRowShapedSettingsTerm, so the new row-result list offered them as tappable results pointing at text no row says any more. Nothing would have caught it: --check is not wired into any gate script or test that I can find. (2) parseSiteAngle GUESSED where it claims to refuse: `44d03m29s S` returned +44.058056, not -44.058056, because the trailing S was taken for a second seconds marker (the string uses d/m letters). That is an 88-degree silent hemisphere error on a string the parser otherwise fully understands. Both repaired. Residuals I checked and deliberately did NOT change: a Google-Maps pair paste ('44.058056, -121.315300') returns null and the field snaps back with no message - still silent, but it is a lat+lon PAIR in one box, outside this finding; and '44,058' is read as 44 degrees 58 minutes (44.966667) rather than a European decimal comma - the comma is a legitimate DMS separator here and the commit-time normalisation shows the operator 44.966667, which is the designed safeguard.
evidence: Staleness: `dart run tools/production/settings_search_index_gen.dart --check` -> 'error: ... settings_search_index.g.dart is stale.' Regenerating produced a 6-line diff, entirely the two Location subtitles (two new 'Decimal degrees or DMS ...' terms in, the two stale 'Positive for ...' terms out) - no other agent's work swept in - and --check now reports 'settings search index is up to date'. The two new terms are 10 words long so isRowShapedSettingsTerm rejects them: they make the section match without adding a new tappable row, which is the right outcome. Parser: a scratch battery printed 'LAT 44d03m29s S -> 44.058055555555555' before the repair and '-> -44.058055555555555' after, with '44d03m29s' still +44.058056 and 'S44d03m29s' still -44.058056. Sever tests: deleting `parse:` from the Latitude row (location_settings.dart:146) took location_dms_entry_test.dart from 11/11 to 8 passed / 3 FAILED; separately forcing `inputFormatters: [_numberFormatter]` back on regardless of `custom` took it to 7 passed / 4 FAILED - so the shipped tests are wired to BOTH production call sites, including the formatter lift, and enterText really does go through the formatter pipeline. Restored: 22/22 across location_dms_entry, settings_picker_controls and file_path_typed_path. Regression sweep: `flutter test test/screens/settings test/golden/public_screenshots_test.dart` = 459 passed / 3 failed; all three are pre-existing - captures_landscape_test.dart is the Windows-captured-goldens-on-Linux debt (fails identically with my edits reverted, 4.38% pixel diff) and public_screenshots_test.dart fails alone with a SequenceLockedException building DashboardScreen, which touches nothing in this shard. flutter analyze on location_settings.dart, settings_text_and_number_inputs.dart and the test: No issues found.
repairSummary: Regenerated packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/settings_search_index.g.dart with `dart run tools/production/settings_search_index_gen.dart` (the fix reworded two indexed subtitles and skipped this on a false premise). In packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/location_settings.dart, parseSiteAngle now decides the trailing-'s' ambiguity by whether the letter is GLUED to a digit as well as by the presence of d/m unit letters, so '44d03m29s' still closes a seconds triple while '44d03m29s S' is read as South instead of being silently stored in the northern hemisphere. Added to test/screens/settings/location_dms_entry_test.dart: a group asserting the index knows the rows accept DMS and no longer carries the deleted subtitles (fails if the regeneration is reverted), and 'a hemisphere written AFTER a d/m/s triple is still a hemisphere' pinning both directions of the ambiguity.
